sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Source scales are normalized to unit variance, with full-column-rank, sign, and lexicographic loading conventions. No loading cap is imposed on the general Fourier or literal-Laplace upper classes; only the fixed lower subclass \(\mathcal M_\star\) requires \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\). The explicitly maintained greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance is recovered from centered empirical characteristic-function moduli on coordinate and pair-sum rays; the uniformly quantified literal-Laplace subclass instead uses clipped fourth cumulants and a global Lipschitz modulus.

project_justification.niche: The upper and lower questions require different scopes. Honest finite-sample regions and upper rates are established on a fixed-dimensional class with known ordinary-smooth ray envelopes and compact spectral and moment bounds, without a global loading cap. The matching lower construction uses an explicit three-variable subclass that separately localizes \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\) and whose witnesses also satisfy the broader Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi published source hypotheses.

prose_updates.related_work: Sanjaroonpouri and Ramazi are the population-identification anchor. Their Assumptions 2--4 use mutually independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources with no Gaussian component, \(1\le k\le p\), unit covariance normalization, lexicographically ordered reduced-loading columns, and full column rank. The general Fourier class used for uniform inference adds known Fourier envelopes and compact spectral and moment restrictions, but no loading cap. The fixed exponent-two lower subclass separately imposes \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\), and its explicit splice witnesses satisfy the published hypotheses, so the logarithmic lower bounds transfer to the published class. No upper rate over the full published class is asserted. The greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition remains explicit in the Fourier model and is verified directly for the witnesses. Belomestny, Trabs, and Tsybakov supply the multivariate characteristic-function polarization precedent, and Meister supplies the scalar fixed-envelope centering and compensated lower-pair architecture; the present proof verifies the six-degree positivity, uniform derivatives, weighted Parseval bound, and causal collision embedding. Wang, Kolar, and Drton study recursive causally sufficient additive-error models and asymptotic coverage of one effect after order and adjustment-set inference; no blanket inclusion relation between their full model and the present one is used. Perkovi\'c, Kalisch, and Maathuis connect background knowledge to IDA effect multisets, while the CRAN \(\texttt{pcalg::ida}\) and Maathuis et al. yeast intervention-ranking workflow motivate reporting an honest compatible-effect set under an audited mixed-noise/Fourier model rather than a selected Gaussian-causal-sufficiency list. Miettinen, Taskinen, Nordhausen, and Oja provide the fourth-cumulant estimating-equation precedent for the literal-Laplace boundary.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The logarithmic upper guarantee is uniform only with fixed dimension and known ray exponents, Fourier envelopes, spectral bounds, and an eighth-moment bound; it does not require a global loading cap. The lower splice uses a fixed three-variable exponent-two class with the separate localization \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\) and conservative numerical constants. Its derivative and weighted-Parseval estimates establish product indistinguishability but do not provide adaptation to unknown smoothness or a matching upper theorem over the unrestricted Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The theorem-level deliverables are the exact ideal representation, collision-stable Lipschitz transfer, measurable finite-sample covariance and whole-fiber regions, \(O((\log N)^{-1})\) expected error on the cap-free Fourier class, the explicit positive smooth-splice pair, matching fixed-subclass minimax and honest-diameter results, lower-only transfer to the Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi class and every superclass containing the fixed splice class, and the uniformly quantified literal-Laplace boundary. The general Fourier and literal-Laplace upper results use no loading compactness; only \(\mathcal M_\star\) carries the direct bound \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3\). No blanket nonnestedness theorem is claimed. The broader published class receives no upper-rate claim because it does not impose the uniform Fourier envelopes or compact spectral and moment bounds used by the estimator analysis. The proposal also does not claim adaptation to unknown exponents, growing-dimension guarantees, polynomial-delay ideal enumeration, correct singleton selection, or minimax sharpness for every exponent profile. When the partial order is total, the ideal family has one treatment-predecessor set and the fiber reduces to the usual singleton regression effect.
